newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays weak, NY fails to inspire.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays weak, NY fails to inspire.

text.p: London's white sugar market stayed weak across the board and traders tidied up spot positions before the December expiry.
Ranges were tight at a maximum $1.40 and turnover was dominated by the December/March switch, boosted by crossed and against actuals trades.
Traders said the dull performance on New York's raws market did not help London, where sentiment was bearish and December was expected to slide further towards $300 support before expiry on Friday.

At 1535 GMT December stood $1.20 lower at $302.60 and March $1.30 down at $302.00, leaving little room for manoeuvre on the Dec/March spread which traders said would probably finish at even money by the end of the week.
Overall market volume reached a light 1,283 lots.
Market sources said Polish white sugar was likely to feature in the physical deliveries against the December expiry as freight orders had already been issued for Polish ports.
Elsewhere, a total 103,150 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 47.098 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at this week's EU tender.
All values lost ground in Paris where volume totalled 702 lots. December was 60 cents lower at $303.40 and March down by the same amount at $302.00.
